current.headline: Hiragana: the 46 sounds that build Japanese
current.summary: Forty-six characters, arranged in a neat grid of vowels and consonants. Learn the pattern and the whole script falls into place, a row at a time.

text.t: Hiragana is the first script every Japanese child learns, and it is the one you will read most. Every word in Japanese can be written in hiragana, even when it is usually written in kanji. Children's books are written almost entirely in it.
There are 46 basic characters. That may sound like a lot, but they follow a grid that makes them far easier to learn than 46 random shapes.
Every row starts with a consonant, and every column is one of the five vowels: a, i, u, e, o. Read across a row and you get that consonant with each vowel in turn.
